goals: Mechanistic: quantify how water partitioning (ET, runoff, drainage, snowmelt) varies with elevation across the Bow River headwaters
Validation: compare simulated partitioning/snow to in-domain observations

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM can simulate partitioning and snow, but the requested elevation gradient cannot be forced correctly in this domain.

answerable: Soil-texture control on partitioning under a single, non-elevation-resolved forcing (does NOT answer the elevation question, and would be a conceptual side-study)

not_answerable.aspect: Elevation-resolved water partitioning across the 1200-3400 m gradient
not_answerable.why: Domain is outside CONUS, so NLDAS-2 (elevation-differentiating) is unavailable; forcing falls back to Qian T62 ~1.9deg, a single cell over the whole basin with no lapse rate. Columns at different elevations receive near-identical precip/temperature, so an elevation-stratified sample would isolate soil, not elevation/climate. The rain-snow transition — the dominant partitioning control here — would be flat across the gradient.
not_answerable.needs: elevation-resolved forcing for Canada (e.g. downscaled ERA5/RDRS or a lapse-rate scheme outside CONUS)

not_answerable.why: SNOTEL is US-only (absent here); ECCC gauges are not ingested by the stack; and streamflow gauges would require routing the single-column stack cannot do.
not_answerable.needs: ECCC/Canadian observation ingest; runoff routing/aggregation for gauge comparison

sampling_strategy.approach: not designed — primary mechanism not representable

bands: blocked: forcing is uniform over the basin, so bands do not separate a climate signal

sampling_strategy.n_justification: No defensible elevation sample exists without elevation-resolved forcing; placing columns by elevation would mislabel a soil signal as an elevation signal.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: N/A — deferred until Canadian elevation-resolved forcing exists

validation_design.comparison: none — SNOTEL is US-only and does not cover Alberta
none — ECCC gauges are not ingested by the stack, and single-column ELM has no routing to produce integrated streamflow

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: none — question infeasible as posed on current stack

requires_capabilities.capability: elevation-resolved forcing outside CONUS (e.g. RDRS/ERA5-Land downscaling or an orographic lapse-rate scheme for Canada)
requires_capabilities.why: The elevation partitioning signal is carried by precip/temperature vs elevation; Qian T62 fallback is a single ~1.9deg cell with no lapse rate
Only Canadian gauges exist in-domain; none are currently ingested
Single-column ELM cannot produce integrated streamflow for gauge comparison

assumptions: The bbox (-115.6,50.7,-114.0,51.4) lies entirely outside CONUS, so NLDAS-2 is unavailable and Qian T62 is the only forcing.
If elevation-resolved partitioning were pursued, spin-up years would also be required for any recharge/water-table target.
open_questions: Can a Canadian elevation-resolved forcing product (RDRS-CaSR, ERA5-Land) be ingested? That is the single unlock for this question.
Would the user accept a conceptual soil-texture partitioning study under uniform forcing as an interim deliverable, understanding it does NOT resolve elevation?
Are any ECCC snow-pillow / snow-course records available that could be added to the observation layer for later validation?
